questiontext:
Consider the function f(x,y)={{CT:0}}.

In this exercise you are first required to find all the critical points (by solving the system of equations \(\nabla f = (0,0)\)) and then classifying them according to the second derivative test. For each critical point the second derivative test will yield one of four possible results: (1) a local maximum. (2) a local minimum or (3) A saddle point (and hence neither a minimum nor a maximum) (4) the second derivative test is undecidable.

Note: If the second derivative test does not give any information (for functions of two or three variables this happens exactly when the determinant of the Hessian matrix is zero) you should enter (4) -- even if you happen to know by some other method whether it is a local minimum a local maximum or neither of these.

You should enter your answer: as a \(\ell \times 3\) matrix where \(\ell\) is the number of critical points. In each line use the first two numbers to enter the \(x,y\) coordinates of one critical point and the third number to indicate the second derivative test classification of this point. For example: If the function has three critical points A=(0,1), B=(2,3) and C=(4,5). And if you the second derivative test classifies them as follows: A is a local minimum, B is a local maximum and C is undecided then you should enter:

matrix([0,1,2],[2,3,1],[4,5,4])

In the feedback window you should see a \(3 \times 3\) matrix corresponding to this input. Of course you are not required to enter the critical points according to any particular order. In the above example matrix([2,3,1],[0,1,2],[4,5,4]) would also be a good answer.

[[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]

How to enter: a square root as sqrt(...), e.g. sqrt(5*x). Other roots as a power, with brackets around the exponent: \(\sqrt[3]{x+1}\) is entered as (x+1)^(1/3).

Outline: Find all critical points by solving \( abla f=(0,0)\), then compute the Hessian determinant \(D=f_{xx}f_{yy}-f_{xy}^2\) and \(f_{xx}\) at each of them.
Step 1 — The critical points

\[ f_x={{CT:1}},\qquad f_y={{CT:2}} \]

[[if test="{{CT:25}}"]]\(f_x=-2-2x=0\) gives \(x=-1\), and \(f_y=4-8y=0\) gives \(y= rac12\).[[elif test="{{CT:26}}"]]From \(f_y=x^3-8=0\) we get \(x=2\); then \(f_x=3x^2y+24x=12y+48=0\) gives \(y=-4\).[[elif test="{{CT:27}}"]]Since \(e^{4y-x^2-y^2}\gt 0\), \(f_x=0\) only when \(x=0\), and \(f_y=0\) only when \(4-2y=0\), that is \(y=2\).[[elif test="{{CT:28}}"]]\(f_x=2x(1+y)=0\) gives \(x=0\) or \(y=-1\). If \(x=0\), then \(f_y=2y+x^2=0\) gives \(y=0\). If \(y=-1\), then \(x^2=2\), so \(x=\pm\sqrt2\).[[elif test="{{CT:29}}"]]\(f_y=2y(x+1)=0\) gives \(y=0\) or \(x=-1\). If \(y=0\), then \(f_x=6x^2+10x=2x(3x+5)=0\) gives \(x=0\) or \(x=- rac53\). If \(x=-1\), then \(f_x=6-10+y^2=0\) gives \(y=\pm2\).[[elif test="{{CT:30}}"]]\(f_x=y-2=0\) and \(f_y=x-1=0\) give the single point \((1,2)\).[[elif test="{{CT:31}}"]]\(f_x=y(1-2x-y)\) and \(f_y=x(1-x-2y)\). If \(x=y=0\) we get \((0,0)\); if \(y=0 e x\), then \(1-x=0\), giving \((1,0)\); if \(x=0 e y\), then \(1-y=0\), giving \((0,1)\); if \(x,y e0\), then \(1-2x-y=0\) and \(1-x-2y=0\), so \(x=y= rac13\).[[/if]]

So the critical points are

Step 2 — The second derivative test

\[ f_{xx}={{CT:4}},\qquad f_{xy}={{CT:5}},\qquad f_{yy}={{CT:6}},\qquad D=f_{xx}f_{yy}-f_{xy}^2={{CT:7}} \]

Second derivative test: \(D\gt 0\) and \(f_{xx}\lt 0\) gives a local maximum, \(D\gt 0\) and \(f_{xx}\gt 0\) a local minimum, \(D\lt 0\) a saddle point, and \(D=0\) means the test is inconclusive.
